rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states a step that a human participant performs, such as choosing or collecting input, and that step is followed by a separate later step that begins only after it is completed: Model the human step as a bpmn:userTask placed as a direct child of the process or subprocess that contains it, connected by sequence flows to the steps before and after it. Inside a userTask, allow only its own resource-related children (resourceRole, performer, humanPerformer, potentialOwner, correlationSubscription, supports), in that schema order. Never place another task, gateway, event, or sequence flow inside a userTask or inside one of its resource-related children.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states a step that a human participant performs, such as choosing or collecting input, and that step is followed by a separate later step that begins only after it is completed

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that some items are required to make an intermediate product or means, and that this product is then needed to obtain other items, so a prerequisite chain exists among the items: Model a task that produces the required intermediate product after the prerequisite items have been obtained and before the step that obtains the dependent items, placed on the sequence flow so the dependent step follows it. Do not leave the dependency only in a label, and do not run the dependent step in parallel with the prerequisite production. If the description says that further intermediate products may be needed, add an exclusive gateway with a 'yes' flow looping back to the production task and a 'no' flow continuing to the dependent step.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that some items are required to make an intermediate product or means, and that this product is then needed to obtain other items, so a prerequisite chain exists among the items

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states an action on an object and then attaches a phrase giving its place, method, or the aspects it is checked against (for example, a list of criteria or a qualifying condition on where or how the action is done): Model the task with a label containing only the core verb and object taken from the description, and move the place, method, or criteria phrase into the task's documentation. Do not let the label carry the qualifier, and do not drop the qualifier from the model, since it belongs in the documentation.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a participant is informed or notified whenever some occurrence is reached, and the notification is an action the process performs on a recipient

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description names two roles, one of which supplies choices or requirements that a separate automated agent then acts on to perform the later steps of the same process: Keep all steps of the process in one participant pool. Create one lane for each named role, including the automated agent, and place each start event, task and gateway in the lane of the role that performs it. Put the starting event in the lane of the role that initiates the process, and put the later performed steps in the lane of the automated agent. Do not omit the lanes, and do not split these roles into separate pools.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description names two roles, one of which supplies choices or requirements that a separate automated agent then acts on to perform the later steps of the same process

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a participant first has to identify or decide which of several items they want, as a preparatory step before further work on those items begins: Model that identification as a user task on the sequence flow directly after the process start event and before the first step that depends on the chosen items. Do not omit it, and do not model it as a second start event that stands beside the process start.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a participant first has to identify or decide which of several items they want, as a preparatory step before further work on those items begins

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that an autonomous actor (such as a bot) performs activities after a user starts it, and that the user may perform another action at any time while those activities run, or that an external event may interrupt them: Model the user-initiated action or the interrupting event as an event subprocess or a boundary event attached to the actor's activity, placed in the lane of the autonomous actor that performs the activity. Do not model it as a separate subprocess or task in the user's lane, and do not add a separate pool for the actor.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that an autonomous actor (such as a bot) performs activities after a user starts it, and that the user may perform another action at any time while those activities run, or that an external event may interrupt them

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description names a step with a specific verb and object, and the candidate task label would replace that verb or object with a synonym: When the description states a step with a verb and object, name the task with that same verb and object, keeping the description's word choice. Do not swap in a synonym that changes the verb, because the paraphrase can drift from what the description says the step does.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description names a step with a specific verb and object, and the candidate task label would replace that verb or object with a synonym

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description has the player's own actions directed at other parties (such as contacts or friends the player selects) that those parties receive, and the description attributes no behavior, response or activity of their own to them: Do not create a pool for those parties. Model each action the player takes toward them as a task in the player's lane, in the order the description states, and do not add a message flow to a separate pool unless those parties are described as performing or responding to something.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description has the player's own actions directed at other parties (such as contacts or friends the player selects) that those parties receive, and the description attributes no behavior, response or activity of their own to them
